status: ALL PROPOSED — awaiting selection. Nothing in this register has been implemented.
note: Suggestions are project design, not official NFL guidance. Each is tied to a measured finding or an observed official page response.
decision_path: 1. Read the problem and the evidence link.
2. Compare the options on impact, cost and risk.
3. Pick one option (or reject the suggestion) and record the date and reason.
4. Only then open an implementation task in COORDINATION.md.

suggestions.title: Score every published benchmark against a fixed naive baseline, on the same rows
suggestions.problem: The site currently publishes accuracy-looking numbers without a baseline, so a reader cannot tell skill from a dumb rule. Measured Week 9: B0 favourite 86.7%, naive point-differential rule 86.7%, naive win-percentage rule 92.3%.

options.label: Keep as-is
options.impact: Readers may mistake a baseline artefact for skill.
options.risk: High — this is the project's core failure mode.

options.label: Always show a baseline column next to every score
options.impact: Skill and luck become visually separable at a glance.
options.cost: Low — one extra computed column per table.

options.label: B + a per-row verdict label ("beats baseline / ties baseline / loses")
options.impact: Makes the conclusion explicit instead of inferable.

suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the baseline set (point differential, win percentage, always-home) as the canonical comparison group.

suggestions.title: Split the competition into a price-free accuracy track and a separate betting track
suggestions.problem: G5 (verified operator price), G7 (net expected value) and G8 (settled ledger) are permanently BLOCKED because no verified prices exist. Result: 0 of 8 strategies can ever be rewarded, and the leaderboard is an empty table by construction.
suggestions.evidence: analysis/validation-gates.json (G5/G7/G8 BLOCKED, eligible_strategies 0); data/flagged.json A01, A08.

options.label: Leave all gates coupled
options.impact: Leaderboard stays permanently empty; no research is ever rewarded.
options.risk: High — the reward mechanism the project asks for cannot function.

options.label: Track 1 = forecast accuracy and calibration (no prices); Track 2 = betting edge (prices required)
options.impact: Track 1 becomes judgeable immediately from official results; Track 2 stays honestly blocked.

options.label: B + publish Track 1 scores for the existing 15 Week 9 lines as a pilot
options.impact: First real, verifiable leaderboard entries this week.
options.risk: Medium — must be labelled a single-slate pilot, not a ranking.

suggestions.recommendation: B, then C as a labelled pilot
suggestions.decision_needed: Choose whether price-free accuracy is a legitimate basis for paper reward points.

suggestions.title: Make the site regenerate on a schedule and show its own staleness
suggestions.problem: The published dashboard is frozen at 2026-11-04 (Week 9 pre-game) while the league is in Week 10. There is no on-page indicator of how stale the numbers are, and no scheduled refresh touches them.
suggestions.evidence: data/audit-snapshot.json as_of=2026-11-04 vs official Week 9 finals on https://www.nfl.com/scores/2026/week-9 (retrieved 2026-11-14); .github/workflows/audit.yml runs a validator, uploads an artifact, and never republishes the site.

options.label: Nothing
options.impact: Site silently drifts further from reality every week.

options.label: Add a "data as of / weeks behind" banner computed from the snapshot date
options.impact: Reader instantly knows the numbers are historical.

options.label: B + a scheduled job that re-runs verification and fails loudly when the snapshot lags
options.risk: Medium — needs a maintainer to fix failures.

suggestions.decision_needed: Approve a publish path that updates the site (not just an artifact) and a maximum acceptable staleness.

suggestions.title: Replace the depth-chart ambition with an honest availability signal
suggestions.problem: The requested 2nd/3rd/4th-string tracking cannot be built from official sources: nfl.com returns 404 for depth charts and publishes no snap counts or role data. Only position, roster status and injury designation are official.
suggestions.evidence: decision/data/availability-probe.json (AV-1..AV-6, each an observed page response on 2026-11-14).

options.label: Estimate depth order from roster/injury lists
options.impact: Requires inference; violates the project's own no-inference rule and would be indistinguishable from a guess.

options.label: Publish an official availability table only (position, designation, participation) and leave string depth blank + flagged
options.impact: Truthful and useful: which positions a club has lost, not who replaces whom.
options.cost: Low — data already captured this session (114 rows).

options.label: B + positional concentration metric (count of Out/Doubtful/Questionable per position group per team)
options.impact: Turns availability into a comparable, source-linked number without inventing depth.

suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the project will accept "positions lost" instead of "2nd/3rd-string replacement" until an official depth source exists.

suggestions.title: Adopt a standing anti-luck evaluation protocol as a written rule
suggestions.problem: A single week produced p=0.007 against a coin flip for the benchmark, which looks like skill and is a false positive by construction when 12+ variants are registered.
suggestions.evidence: decision/results/w9-out-of-sample.json (binomial_p_vs_coinflip 0.007, winner_accuracy 0.867 tied with baseline); analysis/strategies.json (8 registered variants).

options.label: Minimum sample floor + pre-registered family + baseline comparison, no exceptions
options.impact: Most published numbers would become "insufficient evidence", which is correct.

options.label: B + publish a running "number of variants tested" counter used in the adjustment
options.impact: Makes multiplicity visible to the reader.

suggestions.decision_needed: Set the minimum sample floor (e.g. one full season of slates) before any skill label is allowed.

suggestions.title: Put every open question, and its owner, on one decision page
suggestions.problem: Answers are scattered across 6+ session namespaces (origination/, strict/, desk/, evidence-lab/, advisory/, review/) with no single place showing what is decided, what is pending and what is unknowable.

options.label: Leave it in the board
options.impact: Only an agent can find an answer; a human cannot.

options.label: One Decision page: status per question, owner role, source, blocking flag
options.impact: The requested "review and choose the best path" becomes one screen.
options.cost: Low — this session produced the data.

suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the page becomes the canonical place to record decisions.
